name: D.M. 5 luglio 1975 e D.M. 236/1989
references: D.M. 5 luglio 1975 (Ministero della Sanità): altezze minime e requisiti igienico-sanitari dei locali d'abitazione
D.M. 14 giugno 1989, n. 236: prescrizioni tecniche per l'accessibilità, l'adattabilità e la visitabilità degli edifici
note: Italy's national rules for dwellings: DM 5 July 1975 for rooms (heights 2.70 m, 2.40 m for service rooms, bedrooms of 9 and 14 m², a living room of 14 m², openable windows of 1/8 of the floor) and DM 236/1989 for stairs, ramps and doors. The stairs and the doors are a dwelling's own (stairs 0.80 m wide, treads of 25 cm); a common or public stair is 1.20 m wide with treads of 30 cm. A region's own rules go over it as an amendment (it-fvg).

sources.stairs.riser: Practice: a riser of 16 cm with a 30 cm tread gives 2a + p = 62 cm (DM 236/1989, 8.1.10)
sources.stairs.going: DM 236/1989, 8.1.10: tread of at least 30 cm on a common stair
sources.stairs.riser_min: Practice: DM 236/1989 gives no riser, only 2a + p between 62 and 64 cm
sources.stairs.riser_max: Practice: DM 236/1989 gives no riser, only 2a + p between 62 and 64 cm
sources.stairs.going_min: DM 236/1989, 8.1.10: tread of at least 25 cm on a stair that is not common or public (30 cm on one that is)
sources.stairs.step_min: DM 236/1989, 8.1.10: twice the riser plus the tread between 62 and 64 cm
sources.stairs.step_max: DM 236/1989, 8.1.10: twice the riser plus the tread between 62 and 64 cm
sources.stairs.width_min: DM 236/1989, 8.1.10: 0.80 m for a stair that is not common or public (1.20 m for one that is)
sources.stairs.headroom: Not in the standard: a forgiving number (2.10 m)
sources.stairs.flight_rise_max: Not in the standard: a forgiving number
sources.stairs.flight_risers_max: Not in the standard: a forgiving number
sources.stairs.nosing_min: DM 236/1989, 8.1.10: a continuous profile is preferred (a nosing of 2 to 2.5 cm on a discontinuous one)
sources.stairs.nosing_max: DM 236/1989, 8.1.10: a nosing of 2 to 2.5 cm on a discontinuous profile
sources.stairs.open_risers: DM 236/1989, 8.1.10: the riser is inclined to the tread, a continuous profile preferred
sources.stairs.uniformity: Practice: DM 236/1989, 8.1.10 asks a limited and constant pitch and gives no tolerance
sources.stairs.guard_min: DM 236/1989, 8.1.10: a guard of at least 1.00 m, not passed by a sphere of 10 cm
sources.ramps.slope_max: DM 236/1989, 8.1.11: a slope of no more than 8%
sources.ramps.run_rise_max: Not in the standard: a forgiving number
sources.ramps.width_min: DM 236/1989, 8.1.11: 0.90 m for a wheelchair (1.50 m for two people to pass)
sources.ramps.landing_length_min: DM 236/1989, 8.1.11: a level landing of 1.50 x 1.50 m every 10 m
sources.doors.clear_width_min: DM 236/1989, 8.1.1: a clear width of 80 cm for the door into a building or a dwelling (75 cm for the others)
sources.doors.clear_height_min: Not in the standard: a forgiving number (2.10 m)
sources.doors.leaf_width_max: DM 236/1989, 8.1.1: leaves of no more than 120 cm are preferred
sources.doors.frame_allowance: The project's: what a door type's width loses to its frame
sources.doors.exempt: The project's: rooms whose doors are not held to the clear width
sources.rooms: DM 5 July 1975: art. 1 (heights 2.70 m, 2.40 m for corridors, bathrooms and closets), art. 2 (bedrooms 9 and 14 m², living room 14 m²), art. 5 (openable windows of at least 1/8 of the floor)
